title: Miksi: answering with koska
focus: Miksi asks why. Miksi sinä olet kotona? — Koska olen sairas.
prerequisiteSkills: Kuinka with an adjective: answering about degree

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Why are you at home?”  Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. Miksi asks why. Koska introduces the reason in the answer: Miksi olet kotona? — Koska olen sairas (“Why are you at home? — Because I am ill”). The complete question means “Why are you at home”.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question asking for a reason + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state) + location

parts.formation: Miksi asks for a reason.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Sinä addresses one person informally.
Olla has the singular you-form olet: ole- + -t.
Kotona is the conventional location form meaning at home; learn the complete form.

exercises.prompt: Answer “Miksi te menette?”: choose “Because we are ready.”
exercises.explanation: Plural means more than one in this grammatical pattern. A stem is the part of a word to which an ending is attached. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. A koska-clause is a natural short answer to miksi. Put koska before an ordinary statement with its person and verb. A full answer can repeat the main situation before the because-clause. Here the supporting clauses are provided, so the new decision is reason versus question. The complete reply means “Because we are ready”.
